reasoning: Both sets are strong, disciplined plans with frozen interfaces, golden cases, skill routing and reference caveats carried into the design. B wins on substance. Its Stage 2 judges estimators and portfolios on realised out-of-sample variance, as the user asked; A scores the S2 portfolios on Sharpe after costs. B tests every null on a planted-signal bench before any real data and uses within-date shadow nulls, a sealed one-look holdout and a deflated Sharpe over a permanent model log. It uses the user's ten delisted names as a 40-fact validation check (QUAL-08, TC-25), while A defers them waiting for data the user already gave. B's M1 is a real walking skeleton across all four S1 packages with the app, every roadmap milestone has an Exit, and its planned layouts match the tasks' Writes. B has real flaws. Its build order is encoded as false Depends (M5 depends on M12), so it reads against the IDs. It drops the rented GPU, adds no delisting returns, and keeps some stale text (AD-01, the qfeat pipeline count, the TC-25 exit-type question, the MP noise-variance mismatch). Its spec and architecture are also heavier for a solo learner. A is leaner and easier to read, keeps the user's four stages, handles delisting returns and GPU anonymisation well, and has a clean dependency graph. But M2 is a whole app layer in one lopsided milestone, M2–M8 have no roadmap Exit, several open questions are stale ('no contract sections yet' for types that exist), and the research and models planned layouts contradict the queued tasks.
